To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

apo-con-G is nearly structureless in aqueous solution, whereas con-G bound to Mg2+ exists as an α-helical structure that is stabilized by coordination of Mg2+ to γ-carboxylate groups of Gla3–Gla7 and Gla10–Gla14.
the solution conformation of con-G is an extended random coil in the absence of divalent cations, whereas it is an α-helix in the presence of Mg2+ or Ca2+.

the solution structure of apo-con-G was found to be essentially random coil, while the structure of Mg2+-bound con-G was α-helical, spanning residues 3–16; and the three Mg2+ ions bound in a 1:1:1 ratio to three different Gla residues in a 1,2,3:1,2,4:1,2:1,3:1:1 pattern, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the elucidation of the structural basis for the biological activities of the γ-carbolylated conotoxins, a group of small, highly charged peptides isolated from the venom of the marine snail Conus geographus.
elucidation of the structural basis for the potent antagonism of con-G for NMDA receptor channels.
the development of a new generation of synthetic peptides for use in treating neurological diseases and other disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
con-G exists as an α-helical molecule upon binding of Mg2+, but not Ca2+, and that Gla residues 10, 14, and 7 are critical for the adoption of this conformation.
the α-helix of Mg2+/ con-G is stabilized by the three Mg2+ ions, which bind to the peptide through a combination of direct metal-ligand interactions and indirect metal-mediated hydrogen bonding.
the Gla3, -4, -7, -10, and -14 residues are essential for conformational stability and biological activity of con-G.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Gla residues 3 and 7 are important in the stabilization of the metal ion, whereas Gla residues 10 and 14 are important in defining the conformational changes that occur in apo-con-G upon metal ion binding.
the Gla residues in con-G are essential for the adoption of an α-helical structure, and that the Mg2+-binding properties of con-G are a consequence of the adoption of this helical structure.
the conformational flexibility observed in the apo-form of the peptide was eliminated by binding of divalent cations, resulting in a more rigid α-helical structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure of apo-con-G is not α-helical and that the α-helical structure is stabilized by the presence of two or more divalent cations.
Gla residues 3, 4, 7, 10, and 14 are essential for the α-helical folding of con-G in solution, whereas the Gla residue at position 4 is not required for the tightest binding of Mg2+.
Gla residues are essential for the conformational switch that is induced upon binding of divalent cations.
